meta.source: DOE test procedure for water heaters, 10 CFR Part 430, Subpart B, Appendix E (draw patterns and test conditions); DOE FEMP (typical household use); DOE Buildings Energy Data Book table 8.2.4 (per-person use)
meta.notes: The UEF on a water heater label comes from a 24-hour test with one of four draw patterns, picked by the unit's first hour rating. DOE FEMP calls the medium pattern (55 gallons a day, 20,075 a year) typical household use, so it is the default when you do not enter a household size. Per-person use comes from an older field study (10 Seattle homes, 2.6 people each); it is used only to scale use with household size, and you can change it.

testConditions.source: 10 CFR 430 Subpart B, Appendix E, sections 2.3 and 2.4 (supply 58 °F, outlet 125 °F); 67 °F nominal rise

typicalHouseholdGallonsPerDay.source: DOE FEMP: annual energy use based on the Appendix E test for a unit producing 20,075 gallons of hot water per year; Table 2 lists medium use as 55 gal/day

perPersonGallonsPerDay.source: DOE Buildings Energy Data Book (March 2012), table 8.2.4, from Aquacraft, Residential End Uses of Hot Water in Single-Family Homes from Flow-Trace Analysis (2000); archived copy

femp.source: DOE FEMP Table 1: a 0.95 UEF electric storage water heater uses 3,437 kWh a year at 20,075 gallons (used on /methodology to cross-check our energy formula)
